dorsal root ganglion sensory neurons exposed to high glucose concentrations exhibit increased ROS levels in their axons and decreased MnSOD expression.
diabetic sensory neurons have a reduced capacity to detoxify reactive oxygen species, which leads to axonal degeneration and loss.

the mechanisms of axonopathy in diabetic neuropathy.
the mechanisms of axonal degeneration in diabetic neuropathy.
the development of a new type of nerve agent that targets the peripheral sensory nervous system.

diabetes causes oxidative stress in axons of dorsal root ganglia neurons, which in turn leads to impaired axonal out-growth and abnormal axonal morphology.

diabetes mellitus is associated with an increase in ROS in the axons of sensory neurons.

diabetes is a risk factor for peripheral neuropathy, and that diabetes can induce changes in the axons of sensory neurons that can lead to the development of diabetic neuropathy.

oxidative stress is a key player in the pathophysiology of diabetic neuropathy.
